correctness.rationale: The source characterization supplies a nowhere differentiable seed exactly in the negative Radon--Nikodym case. Affine endpoint correction preserves nowhere differentiability. Dyadic rescaling preserves the seed Lipschitz constant on each support, the quasi-triangle inequality gives the cross-support upper bound, and restriction to individual supports gives the matching lower bound. These estimates prove an isomorphic embedding of \(\ell_\infty\) with closed range. A nonzero coefficient forces nondifferentiability on the corresponding whole support interior.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp structural dichotomy: the differentiability complement is either empty or already contains a closed nonseparable classical sequence space, and every nonzero element in that copy is bad on an interval. This robustifies a single-counterexample theorem and identifies the size of the failure set in a natural ambient Lipschitz space rather than adding a routine parameter variant.
